# Ten decisions need your call before *Tidy 2.4* ships.

Tidy is a fictional command-line tool for cleaning project folders. Each decision below says what happens today, the alternative, and a recommendation; answer on its row, add a note where you disagree, and choose Need context when the case is not enough.

## The decisions

<Records {...decisions} />

## How an approved set is applied

The release tool reads the reply. [See the command it runs](#apply), or [what the terms mean](#terms).

## What is not here

<details>
<summary>41 smaller changes need nobody's call</summary>

Dependency bumps (23), documentation fixes (11) and test-only changes (7). They are in the release notes.

</details>

# The command the release tool runs

It is one long line on purpose, so it can be pasted as it is:

```sh
TIDY_CHANNEL=next TIDY_SIGN_KEY=file:///etc/tidy/keys/release-2024.key tidy release --from v2.3.1 --to v2.4.0-rc.1 --notes-from-merged-prs --provenance --tag next --dry-run --verbose
```

</View>

# Terms the decisions use

<dl>
<dt>Release candidate</dt><dd>A build offered for testing before the release itself.</dd>
<dt>Provenance</dt><dd>A signed statement of which commit and workflow built a package.</dd>
<dt>Channel</dt><dd>A named stream of releases, such as next, that users opt into.</dd>
</dl>
